questions.question: Inertia can be measured by its ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mass.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inertia can be measured by its mass.**
 
• **Mass is a measure of the inertia of the object, for an object, its inertia would depend on its mass.**
 
• **Inertia** is the property of an object by virtue of which it opposes any event that attempts to put the object in motion or to change its velocity.
 
• Therefore, an object at rest would want to continue staying at rest and an object in motion would have a tendency to continue its motion.
 
• The greater the mass of the object will be the tendency to resist the events.
 
• Hence, mass is a measure of the inertia of the object.
 
• **Newton's first law of motion:**
 
 
• It states that **"An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.**" Objects tend to "keep on doing what they're doing." In fact, it is the natural tendency of objects to resist changes in their state of motion. This tendency to resist changes in their **state of motion** is described as inertia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force:**

 
 
• The interaction that after applying to a body changes or try to change the state of motion or state of rest is called** force.**
 
• Force is denoted **by F and the SI unit is Newton (N).**
 
• **Force (F) = Mass (m) x acceleration (a).**

questions.question: Which one of the following element is Monatomic unit?

__
 
• **Gold is a Monatomic unit**__.

 __
 
• Monatomic elements are elements that are stable as single atoms.
 
• For an element to be stable by itself, it must have a stable byte of valence electrons.
 
• The atomic number of a monoatomic element is equal to the number of protons in the element.
 
 
 
• Under standard temperature and pressure conditions, the monatomic elements are the noble gases helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, and radon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gold is the most malleable and ductile metal.**

 
 
• **Symbol: Au**
 
• **Atomic no.: 79**
 
• It is a soft metal and is usually alloyed to give it more strength.
 
• It is a good conductor of heat and electricity and is unaffected by air and most reagents.
 
• The most common gold compounds are auric chloride (AuCl₃) and chloroauric acid (HAuCl₄).

questions.question: What is the power of ‘second’ in the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-2.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **SI unit of acceleration** is **meters/second² (m/s²). **
 
• **Hence, the power of the second is -2 as it is in the denominator.**
 
• Acceleration (a) is defined as the** rate of change in velocity. **
 
• **Velocity is a vector quantity**, and therefore **acceleration is also a vector quantity. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of acceleration**
 
• **Uniform acceleration**
 
 
• When an object is travelling in a straight line with an increase in velocity at equal intervals of time, then the object is said to be in uniform acceleration. The free-falling of an object is an example of uniform acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Non-uniform acceleration**
 
 
• When an object is travelling with an increase in velocity but not at equal intervals of time is known as non-uniform acceleration. Bus moving or leaving from the bus stop is an example of non-uniform acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Instantaneous acceleration**
 
 
• The acceleration of an object at any instant of time is known as instantaneous acceleration.

questions.question: Which of the following is the physical quantity for the expression arc/radius?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** the Plane angle.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The physical quantity for the expression of arc/radius is the Plane angle.**
 
• A plane angle is well known: **one full revolution is 360° or 2π radians.**
 
• **Plane angle-** usually refers to an** angle in a 2-dimensional **figure like a** square, triangle, circle, etc.**
 
• **Solid angle **usually refers to an **angle in a 3-dimensional figure **like a cube, cuboid, sphere, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Linear momentum**

 
 
• ​Linear momentum is the vector quantity and is defined as the product of the mass of an object, m, and its velocity, v. 
 
• The linear momentum formula is given by, **P = m v,** where m=mass, v= velocity.
 
• The units of linear momentum are** kg m/s.**
 
 
 
• **Surface tension​**
 
 
• ​Surface tension can be defined as **the property of the surface of a liquid that allows it to resist an external force, due to the cohesive nature of the water molecules.**
 
• Surface tension,** represented by the symbol γ** (alternatively σ or T), is measured in** force per unit length.**
 
• Its **SI unit is newton per meter and** the** cgs unit of dyne per centimetre.**
 
 
 
• **​Velocity**
 
 
• **​Velocity (v) is a vector quantity** that measures** displacement (or change in position, Δs) over the change in time (Δt).**
 
• Velocity is represented by the equation **v = Δs/Δt.**

questions.question: What is the commercial unit of electric energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kilowatt hour**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kilowatt hour**

 
 
• ** Kilowatt hour** is the commercial unit of **electric energy.**
 
• **kWh **is a common unit of **electrical energy** (kilowatt-hour). It is defined as the amount of **energy **utilised for an hour by a **1kW **appliance.
 
• The** kilowatt-hour **(abbreviated kWh) is a unit of **energy** that represents the **energy **used to generate one **kilowatt **of **power **for one hour.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Although it is not a formal standard unit in any system, the** kilowatt-hour** is frequently employed in ele**ctrical applications**. The unit of electrical energy is the **kWh**, which is the same for **household **and **commercial use**.
 
• **Commercial units** are charged at a separate rate than household units, which is higher. It is mostly used to reduce power usage in factories and other commercial settings.

questions.question: Which of the following has unit m/s²?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration**

 
 
• **The rate at which an object's velocity with respect to time changes is referred to as acceleration**.
 
• A vector quantity is an acceleration (has magnitude and direction both).
 
• **LT-2 or meter per second square(m/s2) is the unit of acceleration.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed** 

 
 
• A scalar quantity, speed is defined as the **magnitude of the rate at which an object's position changes over time.**
 
• **The meter per second (m/s) or LT-1 unit of speed.**
 
 
 
• **Velocity**
 
 
• The pace at which **an object's position changes in relation to a frame of reference is known as its velocity, **which is a **time-dependent quantity.**
 
• A description of **an object's speed and direction of motion is what is meant by its velocity.**
 
• The quantity is a vector.
 
• **The meter per second (m/s) or LT-1 unit of velocity.**
 
 
 
• **Distance**
 
 
• The** International System of Units defines a meter** as the distance unit. It's interesting to note that many other derived units or quantities, such as volume, area, acceleration, and speed, may be constructed using this as the basic unit and a few formulae.
 
• **The meter(m) is the SI unit of length.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a unit of distance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Light year.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **unit **of **length **used to express **astronomical distances **is the **light year**, which is roughly comparable to **5.88 trillion miles** or** 9.46 trillion kilometres.**
 
• According to the** International Astronomical Union (IAU),** a light-year is the distance that light travels in a vacuum in **one Julian year (365.25 days).**
 
• Since "light-year" incorporates the term "year," which designates a unit of measurement for time, it is occasionally misinterpreted as a** unit of time.**
 
• The light-year is most typically used to depict distances to stars and other distances on a** galactic scale**, especially in non-specialist contexts and popular science publications.
 
• The measuring unit most frequently used in professional astronomy is the **parsec**, which is derived from astrometry and equals **3.26 light-years. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Newton: **

 
 
• A **newton **is a unit of **force **in the International System of Units (symbol: N).
 
• **1 kgm/s²** is the force that accelerates a mass of** **one kilogramme** **by one metre per second square.
 
• It is named after **Isaac Newton.**
 
 
 
• **Watt:**
 
 
• **​**The **electrical power **determined in **Watts **is the equivalent of one ampere under one volt of pressure.
 
 
 
• **Joule:**
 
 
• **​**The **work performed **by a **force **of one newton acting through one metre is equivalent to one **joule**, a unit of work or energy in the International System of Units (SI).

questions.question: A non-SI unit called 'nit' is the unit of which of the following photometric quantities used to measure a multitude of light intensity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Luminance.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Luminance:-**

 
 
• **It refers to the amount of light that is emitted, reflected, or transmitted from a surface, object, or scene.**
 
• It is a measure of the brightness of light and is often used in the context of visual perception, photography, and various fields of science and technology.
 
• **Luminance is typically measured in units called "candelas per square meter" (cd/m²) or "nits."** It represents the intensity of light as perceived by the human eye. In simpler terms, it is how bright an object appears to an observer.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Luminous exposure:- **

 
 
• It often referred to simply as "exposure," is a concept used in photography and lighting design to quantify the total amount of light that falls onto a photographic film or image sensor in a camera, or onto a surface in a lighting scenario.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in understanding how light affects the outcome of an image or the illumination of a scene.
 
 
 
• **Luminosity**:-
 
 
• It refers to the total amount of energy radiated by an object or source in the form of electromagnetic radiation, typically including visible light and other forms of energy like infrared and ultraviolet radiation.
 
• It's a measure of the overall brightness or total energy output of an object, often used in astronomy and physics to describe the intrinsic brightness of celestial bodies.
 
 
 
• **Luminous emittance:-**
 
 
• **​**Luminous emittance, also known as luminous exitance, is a term used in lighting and radiometry to describe the amount of visible light emitted or radiated from a surface per unit area.
 
• It is a measure of the brightness or luminous output of a surface and is commonly denoted by the symbol "M" or "Mv" and is measured in units of lumens per square meter (lm/m²) or lux (lx).

questions.question: Which physical unit is defined as the field intensity that produces one newton (N) of force per ampere (A) per meter of conductor?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The physical unit defined as producing** one Newton (N) of force per meter per ampere (A)** of current flowing through it is known as** Tesla.**
 
• The derived **SI unit** of **magnetic flux density**, or the strength of a magnetic field, is the tesla (T).
 
• **One Weber per square meter** is represented by one Tesla.
 
• The **gauss** is the analogous and **obsolete cgs unit**. 
 
• There are precisely **10,000 gauss** in one Tesla.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kelvin** is the unit of **temperature.**
 
• **Coulomb** is the unit of **electric charge**.
 
• **Pascal** is the unit of **pressure.**
 
• **Ampere** is the unit of **electric current.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a unit of energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Newton is a unit of force, not energy.
 
• It is named after Sir Isaac Newton in recognition of his work in classical mechanics.
 
• One Newton is the force required to accelerate a one-kilogram mass by one meter per second squared.
 
• The symbol for Newton is "N".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joule (J)**

 
 
• A Joule is a derived unit of energy in the International System of Units.
 
• It is equal to the energy transferred when applying a force of one Newton over a distance of one meter.
 
• The symbol for Joule is "J".
 
 
 
• **Calorie (cal)**
 
 
• A Calorie is a unit of energy commonly used in food energy content measurement.
 
• It is defined as the amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one gram of water by one degree Celsius.

 Term
 Description

questions.question: The Units of Linear momentum are measured in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kg m/s**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **kg m/s** is the unit of linear momentum in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• Linear momentum is defined as the product of an object's mass and its velocity.
 
• The formula for linear momentum (p) is given by: p = m * v, where m is mass in kilograms (kg) and is velocity in meters per second (m/s).
 
• This unit signifies the quantity of motion an object possesses, which is a vector quantity having both magnitude and direction.
 
• It plays a crucial role in various principles of physics, including the conservation of momentum in closed systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Linear momentum** is a fundamental concept in classical mechanics and is conserved in isolated systems, according to the law of conservation of momentum.
 
• In collisions and interactions, the total linear momentum before the event is equal to the total linear momentum after the event, provided no external forces act on the system.
 
• Linear momentum is also related to force through Newton's second law, which states that the rate of change of momentum of an object is equal to the net force acting on it.
 
• Understanding momentum is essential for analyzing various physical phenomena, including motion, collisions, and the behavior of objects under different forces.

 __
 
• It is the **result of stress** experienced by the body.
 
• It may be observed in the **form of physical deformation** undergone by the body.
 
• It can be measured as the ratio of change in dimension to the original dimension.
 
• So it is **unitless**.
 
 
 
• **Work**__
 __
 
• It is a measure of energy expended to move an object over a certain distance.
 
• It is expressed as the **product of the force**(required to move the object) **and the displacement.**
 
• So its dimensions are **ML²T⁻²**.

• So its dimensions are **MLT⁻².**

• **The yard **is a unit of length in both the British imperial and US customary systems, equivalent to 3 feet or 36 inches. Since 1959, it has been internationally standardized as precisely 0.9144 meters by agreement.

questions.question: Which one among the following measures the same quantity as that is measured by the SI unit ‘pascal’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tor**r__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Torr** is a non-SI unit of pressure with a ratio of 760 to 1 standard atmosphere.
 
• It is defined as exactly 1/760 of a standard atmosphere (101325 Pa).
 
• Thus one torr is exactly 101325/760 pascals (≈ 133.32 Pa).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Joule**
 
 
 
• It is an SI unit of work or energy.
 
• It is equal to the work done by a force of one newton acting through one meter.
 
 
 
 

 **Newton**
 
 
 
• It is an SI unit of force.
 
• One newton is the force needed to accelerate one kilogram of mass at the rate of one meter per second squared in the direction of the applied force.
 
 
 
 

 **Watt**
 
 
 
• It is an SI unit of Power.
 
• It is equal to one joule of work performed per second, or to 1/746 horsepower.

questions.question: The loudness of sound is measured in which unit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decibel (dB)**__

 
• **Decibel (dB)** is the unit used to measure the loudness of sound.
 
• The decibel scale is a logarithmic scale that quantifies sound intensity.
 
• Sound levels are often measured in decibels using a sound level meter.
 
• The threshold of hearing is typically set at 0 dB, while sounds above 85 dB can potentially cause hearing damage over prolonged exposure.

 
• **Watt/sq. Metre (w/m2)** is a unit of sound intensity, not loudness.
 
• **Hertz (Hz)** measures the frequency of sound waves, not their loudness.
 
• **Sound intensity** is the power carried by sound waves per unit area in a direction perpendicular to that area, typically measured in watts per square meter.
 
• The decibel scale is used because the human ear perceives sound intensity logarithmically, meaning each 10 dB increase represents a tenfold increase in intensity.
